distractors.reason: 'Highly' usually modifies evaluative adjectives (highly unlikely, highly controversial). We don't normally say 'highly concerned'.
'Heavily' suggests weight or physical intensity (heavily armed, heavily loaded). It does not describe strong emotion.
'Widely' means extensively known or spread (widely read). We don't say 'widely concerned' to express personal worry.

example_sentence: Journalists were ___ concerned about the leaked report.
l1_interference: Falantes de português costumam traduzir 'muito preocupado' como 'very concerned' ou 'highly concerned'. Para a preocupação intensa, o advérbio natural em inglês é 'deeply', assim como em 'profundamente preocupado'.
explanation: In English, certain adjectives combine with specific adverbs. 'Deeply' expresses strong emotion, so it pairs naturally with 'concerned', 'moved', or 'worried'.

related_collocations.example: It is highly unlikely that the deal will be approved.
The editor was fully aware of the risks.
Many readers were strongly opposed to the new policy.

memory_tip: DEEPLY = strong feeling (deeply concerned, deeply moved) | HIGHLY = degree of likelihood or quality (highly unlikely, highly rated)
